stories.title: New index identifies tumor origins
stories.summary: The Clonal Relatedness Index can determine if tumors in the same patient share a common origin. Published in The Journal of Molecular Diagnostics, the findings aim to assist in managing complex digestive and abdominal cancers. It is a new way to track where a tumor actually began.

stories.title: Antibody therapy reverses diabetes in mice
stories.summary: Researchers at UC Davis Health identified mechanisms behind an experimental antibody that reverses type 1 diabetes in mice. The study, published in the journal Diabetes, could influence future treatment development for patients with acute cases of the disease. Mice are currently the primary beneficiaries of this research.

stories.title: Genomic testing often misses cancer mutation targets
stories.summary: Researchers at the NIHR Biomedical Research Centre in Cambridge found that half of targetable cancer mutations are located in the wrong cancer type. Current testing is often organized by where a tumor originates rather than its DNA. Substantial opportunities for targeted treatments are being overlooked annually.

stories.title: Sibeprenlimab preserves kidney function in IgA nephropathy
stories.summary: A UAB study found that sibeprenlimab preserved kidney function over two years in patients with IgA nephropathy. The drug blocks a protein involved in producing abnormal antibodies. Only one patient receiving the treatment experienced a major kidney event, compared with 28 patients in the placebo group.

stories.title: Flu vaccine linked to lower dementia risk
stories.summary: A study in the Annals of Geriatric Medicine and Research suggests that flu shots may help older adults stay sharp. Vaccinated adults were less likely to experience signs of dementia. Brain health remains a primary concern for those seeking to maintain their independence as they age.

stories.title: CAR T-cell therapy explored for lupus
stories.summary: CAR T-cell therapy, which engineers a person's own cells to attack specific targets, is an established treatment for certain blood cancers. Recent research indicates the therapy may also be effective for conditions beyond cancer. The medical field is currently testing its reach.

stories.title: Scientists develop new scaffold for cancer drug
stories.summary: Scientists at the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science have developed IHMT-HPK1-550, a small-molecule inhibitor with a novel scaffold. The candidate compound is intended for cancer immunotherapy. Findings were published in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry on October 28.

stories.title: Personalized lung cancer treatment advances
stories.summary: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer death in the United States, but outcomes are improving for some patients. As Lung Cancer Awareness Month highlights new care methods, thoracic oncologist Marina Garassino is working to push the field toward more personalized treatment options.

stories.title: Tumor vaccine extends survival in glioblastoma patients
stories.summary: A retrospective study from Tokyo Women’s Medical University found that an autologous tumor vaccine extends survival for glioblastoma patients when added to standard protocols. The analysis covered 375 surgical patients treated between 2006 and 2021. Glioblastoma is the most aggressive primary brain malignancy in adults.

stories.title: ICMR survey finds high anemia rates in women
stories.summary: A national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research found that over half of women of reproductive age are anemic. Nearly two-thirds of adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12. The findings highlight a nutritional challenge that extends beyond iron deficiency across the country.

stories.title: India Records A 38% Drop In TB Deaths: What Is Driving The Decline And Why Is Elimination Still A Challenge - News18
Varanasi hospitals investigated for Ayushman Bharat violations
stories.summary: Officials in Varanasi are recommending action against 14 private hospitals for irregularities under the Ayushman Bharat scheme. Complaints included incorrect billing and charging patients for covered services. The district has 214 hospitals registered under the program, and some are now facing removal.

stories.title: Dengue risk model shows limited accuracy
stories.summary: A geospatial index designed to map dengue susceptibility in northern India showed a weak correlation with actual cases in Gorakhpur during 2025. Researchers integrated satellite data and environmental factors to build the model. It successfully identified spatial clusters but struggled to predict reported infection outcomes.

stories.title: ICMR reports high anemia prevalence in women
stories.summary: The ICMR-NIN survey found that over 50 percent of Indian women aged 15 to 49 are anemic. The study used venous blood testing, which is considered the gold standard for population-level health surveys. Debate continues regarding how the condition is measured and classified in India.

stories.title: New survey reports lower anemia prevalence
stories.summary: The ICMR released findings from its 2023 to 2025 survey, which reported lower anemia prevalence than previous national studies. The survey used venous blood sampling and automated analyzers. This method is described as more accurate than the finger-prick tests used in earlier national health surveys.

stories.title: ICMR survey finds anaemia in over half of Gujarat’s young children, ‘model state’ claim questioned by Congress - Telegra
FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri
stories.summary: The FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a water sample showed bromate levels at 12 micrograms per litre, exceeding the limit. The company maintains its water is safe. A sanction allows the regulator to take the case to court, but it is not a conviction.

stories.title: India reaches HPV vaccine milestone
stories.summary: The World Health Organization commended India for administering over 10 million doses of the HPV vaccine to girls aged 14. The milestone reflects efforts to prevent cervical cancer. The organization emphasized the importance of continued access to the vaccine as a tool for cancer prevention.

stories.title: Trial finds no benefit from prehospital antibiotics for sepsis
stories.summary: Early antibiotic treatment is considered critical for reducing sepsis mortality. A new study in JAMA found that administering antibiotics in an ambulance provided no mortality benefit compared to standard care in the emergency department. Each hour of delay is still considered a factor in survival.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak in the DRC
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak on May 15, 2026. As of November 18, there have been 11,712 reported cases and 5,720 deaths, with the vast majority of the impact concentrated in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: Gavi plans purchase of experimental Ebola vaccine
stories.summary: Gavi intends to buy up to 1.5 million doses of an experimental vaccine for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, provided the shot proves safe and effective. The alliance has already contributed $40 million to development efforts. There are currently no licensed treatments for this species.

stories.title: Infants account for most meningitis cases as Gaza outbreak grows, WHO says - Arab News
Global vaccine group aims to buy 1.5 million doses of new Ebola Bundibugyo shot for Congo - Reuters
Meningitis cases surge in Gaza
stories.summary: Gaza health officials have declared an epidemic alert after recording 272 meningitis cases in October. This figure is more than eight times the usual monthly rate. Children under one year old account for 71 percent of the cases, and 15 deaths have been reported this year.

stories.title: Gaza health ministry declares meningitis epidemic
stories.summary: The Palestinian Ministry of Health in Gaza has declared an epidemic alert following a surge in meningitis infections. Officials reported 272 cases in October, citing the collapse of water and sanitation infrastructure as a primary driver. Fifteen deaths have been attributed to the disease since January.

stories.title: Gaza health ministry declares ‘epidemic alert’ amid sharp rise in meningitis cases - The Malaysian Reserve
Japan holds first Ebola response drill
stories.summary: Japan conducted a crisis management drill on Tuesday to simulate a domestic Ebola case. The exercise follows the World Health Organization’s international emergency declaration regarding the outbreak in Congo. This is the first time the government has included the disease in its annual infectious disease response drills.

Review examines digital health readiness
stories.summary: A narrative review of fifteen years of clinical literature concludes that patient digital health readiness is a prerequisite for the success of digital medical interventions. The study suggests that rapid integration of artificial intelligence and telehealth cannot deliver therapeutic benefits without addressing these foundational user factors.

stories.title: Study questions digital health security assessments
stories.summary: A comparative investigation published in Health Economics, Policy and Law suggests that incorporating cybersecurity assessments into national reimbursement decisions may create regulatory bottlenecks. The study analyzed frameworks in Germany and Switzerland, noting that such requirements risk acting as barriers to market entry for new digital health technologies.

stories.title: Government launches AI mental health airlock
stories.summary: The AI in Mental Health Airlock programme will bring regulators and innovators together to evaluate AI-enabled mental health technologies. Health innovation minister James Frith stated the initiative aims to support AI development while ensuring patient confidence. The sandbox is part of a Wellcome-funded programme launched in 2023.

stories.title: Ireland works to meet EU health data standards
stories.summary: HIQA is working to align Ireland’s health information sector with the European Health Data Space Regulation, which entered into force in March 2025. The regulation establishes a common framework for the exchange of electronic health data across all 27 European Union member states.

stories.title: Who oversees digital health? Providers face a regulatory maze - Healthcare Dive
Report details digital health service regulation
stories.summary: The OECD reported that 82 percent of member countries offered online digital health services in 2024. A June 2026 survey found that 34 percent of U.S. adults use AI chatbots for health and medical purposes. The World Bank defines digital health as the use of technology to improve health.

stories.title: Study finds systemic barriers for peer support workers
stories.summary: A study in Administration and Policy in Mental Health and Mental Health Services Research found that culturally and racially marginalized peer support workers face structural hurdles in traditional settings. Institutional environments continue to mirror dominant white cultural frameworks, restricting career progression and authentic expression for underrepresented staff members.

stories.title: Canadian mental health outcomes worsened over two decades
stories.summary: Mental health outcomes in Canada worsened across all age groups and sexes between 2002 and 2024, according to a meta-regression analysis of national survey data. The study tracked trends over twenty-two years, mapping prevalence estimates across adolescents, middle-aged adults, and older populations in the Canadian household population.

stories.title: Minnesota and Iowa rank high in mental health spending
stories.summary: Minnesota and Iowa rank in the top 10 nationwide for mental health spending per resident, according to research by Autism360 using 2025 federal data. Iowa spends $401.76 per resident and Minnesota spends $390.26, both exceeding the national average of $187.65. The money has been accounted for.

stories.title: One in four students use AI for mental health support
stories.summary: A University of Bath study of 2,020 students found that one in four used AI for mental health support in the past six months. Many students reported using the tools as a personal therapist or coach when distressed. The technology is now a primary point of contact.

stories.title: Mississippi study links student gambling to mental health
stories.summary: Seven percent of students across eight Mississippi public universities showed signs of a gambling problem, according to a study published in the International Journal of Mental Health and Addiction. Those students were more likely to report mental health issues. Nearly one in four students surveyed gambled regularly.

stories.title: Parents remain skeptical of AI chatbots for children
stories.summary: A study from Harvard and Boston Children’s Hospital published in JAMA Pediatrics found 76 percent of parents are uncomfortable with using AI-powered treatment for their children. Despite a national therapist shortage, parents remain wary of the technology. The chatbots have yet to win over the household.

stories.title: Survey finds discrimination burdens mental health patients
stories.summary: A survey of Australian adults found that 67.7 percent of respondents consider stigma and discrimination more harmful than their underlying psychological conditions. The research evaluated bias across personal and professional settings, concluding that the social response to mental health challenges often carries a heavier burden than the condition.

stories.title: Students increasingly turn to AI for mental health
stories.summary: A University of Bath survey of 2,020 students found 25 percent used AI for mental health support in the past six months. Students with declared disabilities or those reporting significant distress were the most likely to use tools like ChatGPT as a personal therapist or coach.

research.summary: Depression in older adults may be more than a mental health concern. Scientists discovered that accumulating tau protein, a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, was linked to worsening depressive symptoms in people who still had normal memory and thinking abilities.
